correctness.rationale: For p<q prime, N=pq and rows all units, (F*F)ij=c_{pq}(j-i)/phi(N). Since 0<=i,j<q, off-diagonal indices are never divisible by q. The Ramanujan-sum prime formula gives G=a0 I-(p/phi)sum_r u_r u_r*+(1/phi)11*, where a0=q/(q-1) and u_r indicates one mod-p residue class among the q columns. Dividing q=pk+s gives exactly s classes of size k+1 and p-s of size k. On within-class sum-zero vectors, eigenvalue a0; Cauchy gives p equal-class sums equality subspace dimension q-p+1. Orthogonal complement decomposes into (s-1) large-class contrasts at u, (p-s-1) small-class contrasts at v and a remaining 2x2 block with one a0 and trace determining w. Thus claimed full multiset and multiplicities. As u<w<v<a0 when respective sectors present, least is w for s=1 or u for s>=2, reducing to (p-2)/(p-1)+max(s-2,0)/((p-1)(q-1)). When p=2, s=1, the zero vector is (-1)^j; for all odd p minimum positive. Independent direct Fourier Gram and exact-rational eigenvalue formulas were compared for 20 prime pairs p=2,3,5,7,11 and four larger q each, PASS.
